sanskrit: sa mayā gacchatā mārge vinikīrṇo bhayāvahaḥ vane mahati duṣṭātmā dṛṣṭo bhīmabalād dhataḥ
english: He who had scattered terror on the road was seen by me as I traveled — that evil-souled one slain in the great forest by Bhīma's might.

sanskrit: tatrāśrauṣam ahaṃ caitat karma bhīmasya bhārata brāhmaṇānāṃ kathayatāṃ ye tatrāsan samāgatāḥ
english: There, O Bharata, I heard this deed of Bhīma recounted by the brahmanas who had gathered together at that spot.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ vinihataṃ saṃkhye kirmīraṃ rākṣasottamam śrutvā dhyānaparo rājā niśaśvāsārtavat tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard of Kirmira — that foremost of rakshasas — thus slain in battle, the king, absorbed in thought, sighed deeply like one afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhojāḥ pravrajitāñ śrutvā vṛṣṇayaś cāndhakaiḥ saha pāṇḍavān duḥkhasaṃtaptān samājagmur mahāvane
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that the Pāṇḍavas had gone into exile, the Bhojas and the Vṛṣṇis together with the Andhakas came to them in the great forest, those afflicted ones scorched by sorrow.

sanskrit: pāñcālasya ca dāyādā dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cedipaḥ kekayāś ca mahāvīryā bhrātaro lokaviśrutāḥ
english: The heirs of Pāñcāla, and Dhṛṣṭaketu the king of the Cedis, and the Kekayas — brothers of great valor renowned throughout the world.

sanskrit: vane te 'bhiyayuḥ pārthān krodhāmarśasamanvitāḥ garhayanto dhārtarāṣṭrān kiṃ kurma iti cābruvan
english: They went to the Pārthas in the forest filled with anger and indignation, denouncing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and said: "What shall we do?"

sanskrit: vāsudevaṃ puraskṛtya sarve te kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ parivāryopaviviśur dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: All those bulls among kshatriyas, placing Vāsudeva at their head, surrounded and sat down with Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca duryodhanasya karṇasya śakuneś ca durātmanaḥ duḥśāsanacaturthānāṃ bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
english: Vāsudeva said: The earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karṇa, the evil-souled Śakuni — those four with Duḥśāsana as the fourth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve 'bhiṣiñcāmo dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram nikṛtyopacaran vadhya eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Then let us all anoint Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira — one who acts by treachery is worthy of death; this is the eternal law.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pārthānām abhiṣaṅgeṇa tathā kruddhaṃ janārdanam arjunaḥ śamayām āsā didhakṣantam iva prajāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Arjuna then appeased Janārdana, who was angered by the affliction of the Pārthas and seemed ready to burn up all creatures.

sanskrit: saṃkruddhaṃ keśavaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvadeheṣu phalgunaḥ kīrtayām āsa karmāṇi satyakīrter mahātmanaḥ
english: Seeing Keśava so enraged, Phalguna began to recount, based on his knowledge of former births, the deeds of that great-souled one whose glory is true.

sanskrit: puruṣasyāprameyasya satyasyāmitatejasaḥ prajāpatipater viṣṇor lokanāthasya dhīmataḥ
english: Of that immeasurable person, of truthful nature, of limitless splendor — the lord of Prajāpati, Viṣṇu, the master of the worlds, the wise one.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca daśa varṣasahasrāṇi yatrasāyaṃgṛho muniḥ vyacaras tvaṃ purā kṛṣṇa parvate gandhamādane
english: Arjuna said: For ten thousand years, ever going home only at evening, you wandered as a sage of old, O Kṛṣṇa, on Mount Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca puṣkareṣv avasaḥ kṛṣṇa tvam apo bhakṣayan purā
english: For ten thousand years and ten hundred years besides, you dwelt at Puṣkara, O Kṛṣṇa, subsisting on water in former times.

sanskrit: ūrdhvabāhur viśālāyāṃ badaryāṃ madhusūdana atiṣṭha ekapādena vāyubhakṣaḥ śataṃ samāḥ
english: With arms raised, at Badarika in Vishalya, O Madhusūdana, you stood on one foot, subsisting on air, for a hundred years.

sanskrit: apakṛṣṭottarāsaṅgaḥ kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ āsīḥ kṛṣṇa sarasvatyāṃ satre dvādaśavārṣike
english: With upper garment cast aside, emaciated, your veins standing out, you were present, O Kṛṣṇa, at the twelve-year satra sacrifice on the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: prabhāsaṃ cāpy athāsādya tīrthaṃ puṇyajanocitam tathā kṛṣṇa mahātejā divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam ātiṣṭhas tapa ekena pādena niyame sthitaḥ
english: Reaching Prabhāsa, that holy tirtha fit for righteous folk, O Kṛṣṇa of great splendor, you likewise performed austerities there for a divine thousand years, standing on one foot, abiding in discipline.

sanskrit: kṣetrajñaḥ sarvabhūtānām ādir antaś ca keśava nidhānaṃ tapasāṃ kṛṣṇa yajñas tvaṃ ca sanātanaḥ
english: You are the knower of the field in all beings, the beginning and the end, O Keśava; you are the repository of all austerities, O Kṛṣṇa, and you are the eternal sacrifice.

sanskrit: nihatya narakaṃ bhaumam āhṛtya maṇikuṇḍale prathamotpāditaṃ kṛṣṇa medhyam aśvam avāsṛjaḥ
english: Having slain Naraka the son of Earth and recovered the jeweled earrings that were first created, O Kṛṣṇa, you released the pure sacrificial horse.

sanskrit: kṛtvā tat karma lokānām ṛṣabhaḥ sarvalokajit avadhīs tvaṃ raṇe sarvān sametān daityadānavān
english: Having accomplished that deed, O bull of all the worlds, O conqueror of all the worlds, you slew in battle all the daityas and danavas who had assembled.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarveśvaratvaṃ ca saṃpradāya śacīpateḥ mānuṣeṣu mahābāho prādurbhūto 'si keśava
english: Then, having bestowed supreme lordship upon the husband of Śacī, you manifested, O mighty-armed Keśava, among human beings.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ nārāyaṇo bhūtvā harir āsīḥ paraṃtapa brahmā somaś ca sūryaś ca dharmo dhātā yamo 'nalaḥ
english: You, having become Nārāyaṇa, were Hari, O scorcher of foes — Brahmā, Soma, the Sun, Dharma, Dhata, Yama, and Agni.

sanskrit: vāyur vaiśravaṇo rudraḥ kālaḥ khaṃ pṛthivī diśaḥ ajaś carācaraguruḥ sraṣṭā tvaṃ puruṣottama
english: Vāyu, Vaiśravaṇa, Rudra, Time, the sky, the earth, the directions — the unborn, the guru of all that moves and does not move, the creator — you are all these, O Puruṣottama.

sanskrit: turāyaṇādibhir deva kratubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ ayajo bhūritejā vai kṛṣṇa caitrarathe vane
english: With sacrifices beginning with the Turayana and others, with lavish sacrificial fees, you sacrificed with great splendor, O Kṛṣṇa, in the Chaitratha forest.

sanskrit: śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi suvarṇasya janārdana ekaikasmiṃs tadā yajñe paripūrṇāni bhāgaśaḥ
english: A hundred times a hundred thousand measures of gold, O Janārdana — at each one of those sacrifices, that amount was distributed in full as shares.

sanskrit: aditer api putratvam etya yādavanandana tvaṃ viṣṇur iti vikhyāta indrād avarajo bhuvi
english: Having also become the son of Aditi, O joy of the Yādavas, you became renowned on earth as Viṣṇu, younger brother of Indra.

sanskrit: śiśur bhūtvā divaṃ khaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca paraṃtapa tribhir vikramaṇaiḥ kṛṣṇa krāntavān asi tejasā
english: Becoming a child, O scorcher of foes, with three strides you traversed, O Kṛṣṇa, heaven, the sky, and the earth by your splendor.

sanskrit: saṃprāpya divam ākāśam ādityasadane sthitaḥ atyarocaś ca bhūtātman bhāskaraṃ svena tejasā
english: Having reached the heavens and the sky, standing in the abode of the sun, O soul of all beings, you outshone the sun himself with your own radiance.

sanskrit: sāditā mauravāḥ pāśā nisundanarakau hatau kṛtaḥ kṣemaḥ punaḥ panthāḥ puraṃ prāgjyotiṣaṃ prati
english: The nooses of Mura were severed, Nisunda and Naraka were slain, and the road to the city of Prāgjyotiṣa was made safe once more.

sanskrit: jārūthyām āhutiḥ krāthaḥ śiśupālo janaiḥ saha bhīmasenaś ca śaibyaś ca śatadhanvā ca nirjitaḥ
english: Ahuti of the Jaruthya clan, Krātha, Śiśupāla together with his people, Bhīmasena of the Yādavas, Śaibya, and Śatadhanvan — all were defeated.

sanskrit: tathā parjanyaghoṣeṇa rathenādityavarcasā avākṣīr mahiṣīṃ bhojyāṃ raṇe nirjitya rukmiṇam
english: Likewise, with your chariot that roars like a rain-cloud and blazes like the sun, you carried away the chief queen after defeating Rukmiṇī's kinsman in battle.

sanskrit: indradyumno hataḥ kopād yavanaś ca kaśerumān hataḥ saubhapatiḥ śālvas tvayā saubhaṃ ca pātitam
english: Indradyumna was slain in anger, and Kasheruman the Yavana was slain; the lord of Saubha, Śālva, was slain by you, and the Saubha itself was brought down.

sanskrit: irāvatyāṃ tathā bhojaḥ kārtavīryasamo yudhi gopatis tālaketuś ca tvayā vinihatāv ubhau
english: On the Irāvatī likewise, the Bhoja equal in battle to Kārtavīrya, and Gopati and Talaketu — both were slain by you.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca bhogavatīṃ puṇyām ṛṣikāntāṃ janārdana dvārakām ātmasāt kṛtvā samudraṃ gamayiṣyasi
english: That holy Dvārakā, dear to the sages, beloved of the Bhogavatis, O Janārdana — having made it your own, you will send it into the ocean.

sanskrit: na krodho na ca mātsaryaṃ nānṛtaṃ madhusūdana tvayi tiṣṭhati dāśārha na nṛśaṃsyaṃ kuto 'nṛju
english: Neither anger nor envy, neither falsehood nor cruelty dwells in you, O Madhusūdana, O Dāśārha — how then could there be dishonesty?

sanskrit: āsīnaṃ cittamadhye tvāṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā āgamya ṛṣayaḥ sarve 'yācantābhayam acyuta
english: You who sit blazing with your own splendor in the center of the mind — all the sages came to you, O Acyuta, and begged for freedom from fear.

sanskrit: yugānte sarvabhūtāni saṃkṣipya madhusūdana ātmany evātmasāt kṛtvā jagad āsse paraṃtapa
english: At the end of the age, having gathered all beings and absorbed the whole world into yourself, O Madhusūdana, you rest, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: naivaṃ pūrve nāpare vā kariṣyanti kṛtāni te karmāṇi yāni deva tvaṃ bāla eva mahādyute
english: Neither those who came before nor those who will come after could ever accomplish the deeds that you, O god of great splendor, performed even as a child.

sanskrit: kṛtavān puṇḍarīkākṣa baladevasahāyavān vairājabhavane cāpi brahmaṇā nyavasaḥ saha
english: You accomplished all this, O lotus-eyed one, aided by Baladeva, and in the palace of Viraja you dwelt together with Brahmā.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tadātmānam ātmā kṛṣṇasya pāṇḍavaḥ tūṣṇīm āsīt tataḥ pārtham ity uvāca janārdanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to that very soul of Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍava fell silent; then Janārdana spoke to Pārtha:

sanskrit: mamaiva tvaṃ tavaivāhaṃ ye madīyās tavaiva te yas tvāṃ dveṣṭi sa māṃ dveṣṭi yas tvām anu sa mām anu
english: "You are mine alone and I am yours alone; what is mine is yours alone. Whoever hates you hates me; whoever follows you follows me."

sanskrit: naras tvam asi durdharṣa harir nārāyaṇo hy aham lokāl lokam imaṃ prāptau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
english: "You are Nara, O unconquerable one, and I am Hari, Nārāyaṇa; the two sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa have come from that world to this world."

sanskrit: ananyaḥ pārtha mattas tvam ahaṃ tvattaś ca bhārata nāvayor antaraṃ śakyaṃ vedituṃ bharatarṣabha
english: "You are not different from me, O Pārtha, and I am not different from you, O Bharata; no difference between us two can be perceived, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: tasmin vīrasamāvāye saṃrabdheṣv atha rājasu dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhair vīrair bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritā
english: In that assembly of heroes, with the kings aroused in anger, surrounded by heroes led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna and by her brothers —

sanskrit: pāñcālī puṇḍarīkākṣam āsīnaṃ yādavaiḥ saha abhigamyābravīt kṛṣṇā śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇī
english: — Pāñcālī, seeking refuge, approached the lotus-eyed one who sat among the Yādavas, and Kṛṣṇa addressed the worthy refuge-giver.

sanskrit: pūrve prajānisarge tvām āhur ekaṃ prajāpatim sraṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtānām asito devalo 'bravīt
english: "In the primeval creation of creatures they proclaimed you the one Prajāpati, creator of all beings — so Asita and Devala have declared."

sanskrit: viṣṇus tvam asi durdharṣa tvaṃ yajño madhusūdana yaṣṭā tvam asi yaṣṭavyo jāmadagnyo yathābravīt
english: "You are Viṣṇu, O unconquerable one; you are the sacrifice, O Madhusūdana; you are the sacrificer and the object of sacrifice — so Jamadagni's son has declared."

sanskrit: ṛṣayas tvāṃ kṣamām āhuḥ satyaṃ ca puruṣottama satyād yajño 'si saṃbhūtaḥ kaśyapas tvāṃ yathābravīt
english: "The sages call you forbearance and truth, O Puruṣottama; from truth the sacrifice is born — so Kaśyapa has declared of you."

sanskrit: sādhyānām api devānāṃ vasūnām īśvareśvaraḥ lokabhāvana lokeśa yathā tvāṃ nārado 'bravīt
english: "Lord of lords over even the Sādhyas, the gods, and the Vasus; sustainer of the worlds, master of the worlds — so Nārada has declared you to be."

sanskrit: divaṃ te śirasā vyāptaṃ padbhyāṃ ca pṛthivī vibho jaṭharaṃ te ime lokāḥ puruṣo 'si sanātanaḥ
english: "Heaven is pervaded by your head, O lord, and the earth by your feet; these worlds are your belly — you are the eternal Person."

sanskrit: vidyātapo 'bhitaptānāṃ tapasā bhāvitātmanām ātmadarśanasiddhānām ṛṣīṇām ṛṣisattama
english: "For those scorched by knowledge and austerity, whose selves have been purified by penance, who have attained self-vision — for those seers, O best of seers —"

sanskrit: rājarṣīṇāṃ puṇyakṛtām āhaveṣv anivartinām sarvadharmopapannānāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ puruṣottama
english: "— and for the royal sages who have done righteous deeds, who never turn back in battle, who are endowed with all dharmas — you are the ultimate goal, O Puruṣottama."

sanskrit: tvaṃ prabhus tvaṃ vibhus tvaṃ bhūr ātmabhūs tvaṃ sanātanaḥ lokapālāś ca lokāś ca nakṣatrāṇi diśo daśa nabhaś candraś ca sūryaś ca tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: "You are the lord, you are the pervader, you are the earth, you are self-born, you are eternal; the world-guardians, the worlds, the constellations, the ten directions, the sky, the moon, and the sun — all this is established in you."

sanskrit: martyatā caiva bhūtānām amaratvaṃ divaukasām tvayi sarvaṃ mahābāho lokakāryaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: "The mortality of living beings and the immortality of the dwellers in heaven — all the workings of the worlds are established in you, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: sā te 'haṃ duḥkham ākhyāsye praṇayān madhusūdana īśas tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ
english: "I shall tell you my sorrow out of affection, O Madhusūdana, for you are the lord of all beings, both divine and human."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu bhāryā pārthānāṃ tava kṛṣṇa sakhī vibho dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhaginī sabhāṃ kṛṣyeta mādṛśī
english: "How could one such as I — wife of the Pārthas, your friend O Kṛṣṇa, sister of Dhṛṣṭadyumna — be dragged into the assembly hall?"

sanskrit: strīdharmiṇī vepamānā rudhireṇa samukṣitā ekavastrā vikṛṣṭāsmi duḥkhitā kurusaṃsadi
english: "I who follow the dharma of women, trembling, drenched in blood, clad in a single garment, was dragged in distress into the assembly of the Kurus."

sanskrit: rājamadhye sabhāyāṃ tu rajasābhisamīritām dṛṣṭvā ca māṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ prāhasan pāpacetasaḥ
english: "Seeing me in the midst of kings in the assembly hall, afflicted by my monthly course, the evil-minded sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra laughed."

sanskrit: dāsībhāvena bhoktuṃ mām īṣus te madhusūdana jīvatsu pāṇḍuputreṣu pāñcāleṣv atha vṛṣṇiṣu
english: "They sought to enjoy me as a slave-woman, O Madhusūdana, even while the sons of Pāṇḍu lived, and the Pāñcālas, and the Vṛṣṇis."

sanskrit: nanv ahaṃ kṛṣṇa bhīṣmasya dhṛtarāṣṭrasya cobhayoḥ snuṣā bhavāmi dharmeṇa sāhaṃ dāsīkṛtā balāt
english: "Surely I am by law the daughter-in-law of both Bhīṣma and Dhṛtarāṣṭra — yet I have been forcibly enslaved!"

sanskrit: garhaye pāṇḍavāṃs tv eva yudhi śreṣṭhān mahābalān ye kliśyamānāṃ prekṣante dharmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
english: "Yet I blame the Pāṇḍavas themselves — the greatest in battle, the mightily strong — who watched their illustrious wedded wife being tormented."

sanskrit: dhig balaṃ bhīmasenasya dhik pārthasya dhanuṣmatām yau māṃ viprakṛtāṃ kṣudrair marṣayetāṃ janārdana
english: "Shame on Bhīmasena's strength! Shame on Pārtha's archery! That those two could endure, O Janārdana, the outrage done to me by those mean ones!"

sanskrit: śāśvato 'yaṃ dharmapathaḥ sadbhir ācaritaḥ sadā yad bhāryāṃ parirakṣanti bhartāro 'lpabalā api
english: "This is the eternal path of dharma always followed by the good: that husbands protect their wives, even those of little strength."

sanskrit: bhāryāyāṃ rakṣyamāṇāyāṃ prajā bhavati rakṣitā prajāyāṃ rakṣyamāṇāyām ātmā bhavati rakṣitaḥ
english: "When a wife is protected, the offspring is protected; when offspring is protected, the self is protected."

sanskrit: ātmā hi jāyate tasyāṃ tasmāj jāyā bhavaty uta bhartā ca bhāryayā rakṣyaḥ kathaṃ jāyān mamodare
english: "For the self is indeed born in her, and therefore she is called 'jaya' — the wife. And the husband too should be protected by his wife. How then could those born from my womb act thus?"

sanskrit: nanv ime śaraṇaṃ prāptān na tyajanti kadā cana te māṃ śaraṇam āpannāṃ nānvapadyanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "These very ones who never abandon those who come to them for refuge — those Pāṇḍavas did not come to my aid when I sought their refuge."

sanskrit: pañceme pañcabhir jātāḥ kumārāś cāmitaujasaḥ eteṣām apy avekṣārthaṃ trātavyāsmi janārdana
english: "These five sons — born to me from five fathers — are princes of immeasurable might; even for their sake I should be protected, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: prativindhyo yudhiṣṭhirāt sutasomo vṛkodarāt arjunāc chrutakīrtis tu śatānīkas tu nākuliḥ
english: "Prativindhya from Yudhiṣṭhira, Sutasoma from Vṛkodara, Śrutakīrti from Arjuna, and Śatānīka from Nakula —"

sanskrit: kaniṣṭhāc chrutakarmā tu sarve satyaparākramāḥ pradyumno yādṛśaḥ kṛṣṇa tādṛśās te mahārathāḥ
english: "— and Śrutakarman from the youngest — all are of true valor; like your Pradyumna, O Kṛṣṇa, such are those great warriors."

sanskrit: nanv ime dhanuṣi śreṣṭhā ajeyā yudhi śātravaiḥ kimarthaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ sahante durbalīyasām
english: "Surely these men are foremost in archery, unconquerable in battle by enemies — why then do they endure the wrongdoing of the weaker sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra?"

sanskrit: adharmeṇa hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ sarve dāsāḥ kṛtās tathā sabhāyāṃ parikṛṣṭāham ekavastrā rajasvalā
english: "The kingdom was seized by adharma, they were all made slaves, and I was dragged into the assembly hall clad in one garment during my courses."

sanskrit: nādhijyam api yac chakyaṃ kartum anyena gāṇḍivam anyatrārjunabhīmābhyāṃ tvayā vā madhusūdana
english: "The Gāṇḍīva bow cannot even be strung by anyone other than Arjuna, Bhīma, or you, O Madhusūdana."

sanskrit: dhig bhīmasenasya balaṃ dhik pārthasya ca gāṇḍivam yatra duryodhanaḥ kṛṣṇa muhūrtam api jīvati
english: "Shame on Bhīmasena's strength and shame on Pārtha's Gāṇḍīva, if Duryodhana still lives even for a moment, O Kṛṣṇa!"

sanskrit: ya etān ākṣipad rāṣṭrāt saha mātrāvihiṃsakān adhīyānān purā bālān vratasthān madhusūdana
english: "He who drove these boys from the kingdom when they were young and innocent, studying, observing their vows, along with their mother, O Madhusūdana —"

sanskrit: bhojane bhīmasenasya pāpaḥ prākṣepayad viṣam kālakūṭaṃ navaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ saṃbhṛtaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: "— that wicked one mixed poison in Bhīmasena's food — kalakuta poison, fresh and sharp and collected, hair-raising in its power —"

sanskrit: taj jīrṇam avikāreṇa sahānnena janārdana saśeṣatvān mahābāho bhīmasya puruṣottama
english: "— yet that poison was digested by Bhīma without any ill effect along with the food, O Janārdana, O mighty-armed Puruṣottama, because of his surpassing vitality."

sanskrit: pramāṇakoṭyāṃ viśvastaṃ tathā suptaṃ vṛkodaram baddhvainaṃ kṛṣṇa gaṅgāyāṃ prakṣipya punar āvrajat
english: "Then that wretch bound Vṛkodara while he lay trustingly asleep at Pramanakoți and, casting him into the Gaṅgā, returned."

sanskrit: yadā vibuddhaḥ kaunteyas tadā saṃchidya bandhanam udatiṣṭhan mahābāhur bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: "When the son of Kuntī awoke, he cut through his bonds and rose up — that mighty-armed Bhīmasena of great strength."

sanskrit: āśīviṣaiḥ kṛṣṇasarpaiḥ suptaṃ cainam adaṃśayat sarveṣv evāṅgadeśeṣu na mamāra ca śatruhā
english: "He had also set deadly venomous black serpents to bite him as he slept, on every part of his body — yet the slayer of foes did not die."

sanskrit: pratibuddhas tu kaunteyaḥ sarvān sarpān apothayat sārathiṃ cāsya dayitam apahastena jaghnivān
english: "But when the son of Kuntī awoke, he crushed all the serpents and struck down that wretch's beloved charioteer with the back of his hand."
